script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. MILLER & SONS - DAY

JIM MILLER, 50, a distinguished and stern boss, sits at his desk going through piles of papers. His assistant, MELANIE WU, 28, a bright and ambitious employee, enters the room.

MELANIE:
Good morning, Mr. Miller.

JIM:
(Without looking up)
Good morning, Melanie.

Melanie sets down a tray of coffees on his desk. Jim takes a cup, but doesn't say thank you.

MELANIE:
(Setting down her own cup)
The new project proposal is on your desk. I've scheduled a meeting with the team to discuss it this afternoon.

Jim glances at the papers.

JIM:
(Sighs)
Yes, I saw.

Melanie looks around the office, noticing a new employee, SARAH, 24, sitting timidly at her desk.

MELANIE:
(To Sarah)
Hello, I'm Melanie. This is Jim, our boss.

Sarah nods shyly, looking down at her desk.

INT. MILLER & SONS - AFTERNOON

The team gathers around a conference table. Jim sits at the head, Melanie to his right, and the new hires - SARAH, PETER, 31, and JESSICA, 27 - sit around the table.

JIM:
Let's discuss our new project. (Pauses) We've been in the manufacturing business for decades. It's time we innovate and move into the tech industry.

PETER:
But what about our loyal customers? Won't they be confused by the shift?

JIM:
(Leans back in his chair)
Confused or intrigued? We have the opportunity to broaden our reach and appeal to a younger demographic.

JESSICA:
What about the risk? Technology is ever-evolving, and we might not be able to keep up.

JIM:
(Smirks)
Risk is a part of business. And with the right team, we can make it work.

Sarah raises her hand.

SARAH:
Excuse me, Mr. Miller. How do you plan on leading this transition? You've been in manufacturing your entire career.

Jim hesitates, then leans forward.

JIM:
I've been thinking a lot about that. And I believe it's time for me to step out of my comfort zone and learn from you all.

INT. MILLER & SONS - NIGHT

Jim sits alone in his office, looking at the project proposal. He feels a sense of unease and uncertainty, but also excitement. He glances at Melanie's desk, where she's working late.

Melanie notices him watching her and looks up.

MELANIE:
(Smiling)
What keeps you up at night, Mr. Miller?

Jim hesitates, then sits down in the chair across from her.

JIM:
I'm not used to this. The tech industry is new to me. I'm afraid of failing.

Melanie leans forward.

MELANIE:
(Softly)
We all have our fears. But we also have the opportunity to learn, grow, and succeed. You've built a great company, but it's time to evolve. And with a team like this, there's nothing we can't accomplish.

Jim looks at her, a small smile forming on his lips.

JIM:
(Sighs)
You're right, Melanie. Let's do this.

INT. MILLER & SONS - DAY

The team is hard at work, brainstorming ideas for the new project. Jim sits at his desk, watching as Melanie and Sarah work together seamlessly. Peter and Jessica also collaborate, bringing new ideas to the table.

Jim looks around the room, feeling a sense of pride and accomplishment. He realizes that this transition isn't just about the company, but about himself and his identity. He's more than just a boss; he's a leader, a learner, and a part of a team.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
